thread:
harper: Quick update 10Finished canary for the incremental tokenizer cache + batch-aware tokenization. Toplines look good and it's low-risk :tada:

joan: Nice. Topline numbers?

harper: Tokenization p50 down ~65% (was ~15ms -> ~5ms) for common short prompts, p95 tokenization time down ~40%. End-to-end p50 latency improved ~6%, p95 ~9% on short/interactive workloads. Tokenization CPU cycles per-request down ~18% across the canary slice.

devin: Hit rate? what fraction of requests actually reused tokenized prefixes?

harper: For the canary slice, prefix token reuse ~72% when routes have stable system/user context. For stateless workloads it was ~5% (no harm).

bench-bot: Canary details: 48h, env=prod-canary, traffic=6%, workload=interactive-chat, tokenization CPU -18%, overall token compute -3.8%, report: https://redwood-internal/bench/reports/1876543210

maya: Any correctness concerns? tokenizers can be tricky with unicode/normalization.

harper: Absolutely. We added three guards: 1) tokenizer_version embedded in cache key (invalidates on tokenizer/model change), 2) unicode normalization and whitespace normalization tests in the caching path, 3) a stochastic sampling of cached vs uncached outputs with automatic divergence alerts (KL + exact-match for deterministic prompts). Ran fuzz test corpus ~50k inputs; no discrepancies beyond expected sampling variance.

joan: Rollout plan? flags to expose?

harper: Ramp 6% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with automated checks at each step (latency, tokenization divergence, hitrate). We'll expose per-route flags: tokenizer_cache.enabled (bool), tokenizer_cache_ttl_ms (int), and tokenizer_cache_scope (enum: route|organization). Default enabled for Hosted; Dedicated customers can opt-out per-route.

devin: Any perf regressions seen?

harper: A small cold-start jitter on a few CPU-constrained nodes while JITing the tokenizer cache serializer; fixed by prewarming and lazy background snapshotting. No correctness regressions.

ops-bot: Guard configured: runtime/tokenizer_cache/p99_delta > 12% -> auto-fallback. Also added divergence alert if sampled KL > 0.02.

joan: Can we get dashboard panels added? I'd like "Tokenizer Cache Hitrate", "Tokenization CPU Savings", and a per-route divergence panel.

harper: On it. Adding tiles to Runtime Overview and a short-term alert if hitrate drops >25% vs rolling 7d.

maya: Release notes blurb for sales/support?

harper: Draft: "Incremental tokenizer cache reduces tokenization CPU and improves latency for reuse-heavy interactive flows. Typical tokenization latency reduction ~60% for common short prompts; end-to-end p95 improves ~5-10% depending on workload. Per-route opt-out available." Will post in #marketing-launch.

devin: Config snippet for local testing?

harper: Sure, ops/devs can use this snippet:

```
runtime:
  tokenizer_cache:
    enabled: true
    tokenizer_cache_ttl_ms: 60000
    batch_optimize: true
    sample_rate: 1.0  # 0..1 for caching sample
```

joan: Any notes for Dedicated customers about memory use?

harper: Cache stays bounded per-worker; default max ~32MB per worker and evicts LRU. We also support a "max_entries" route override for high-density routes.

bench-bot: Schedule: full-rollout comparison job at 1876620000 to produce final delta numbers for the release notes.

ops-bot: Canary deploy finished 705 . Auto-fallback enabled.

maya: Great work. Could you drop 2 slides + 30s demo clip for tomorrow's all-hands?

harper: Yep dropping slides + a short demo in #all-hands by EOD.

joan: Thanks team :clap:

devin: Nice win, low-risk and good ops story.

harper: Thanks all, tagging eng-sre for 25% ramp watch.
